name: Braised Lamb Ribs with Apricots and Onions

ingredients.name: A few tablespoons of oil for sautéing
ingredients.prep: some trimmed off pieces of lamb fat

instructions.primary_message: Trim off the some of the A few tablespoons of oil for sautéing pieces of lamb fat. Thinly slice the onions.
instructions.secondary_message:
A few tablespoons of oil for sautéing
2 medium onions

instructions.primary_message: In a small bowl, mix the ingredients for the spice rub. Sprinkle spice rub evenly on both sides of lamb ribs and set aside.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and add oil or lamb fat. Sauté onions until they're softened but not browned, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.

To assemble the braise: Cover the bottom of your pan with sautéed onions and apricots. Nestle rack of ribs into onions and apricots. Pour in enough water so that the ribs are 1/3 of the way submerged, about 2 cups. Cover the pan with foil.

In the meantime, preheat oven to 275°F. Braise ribs in oven until very tender, about 3 hours. Uncover pan and turn heat to 375°F. Continue braising until the fat on the surface is browned and onions are very brown, about 30 minutes longer. Pour off rendered lamb fat in the pan, setting it aside for another use.
Serve hot or warm. Leftovers may be reheated in a 250°F oven until warm, about 30 minutes.

assumed: A few tablespoons of oil for sautéing, some trimmed off pieces of lamb fat

schema_metadata.keywords: lamb, lamb ribs, mains, The Nasty Bits

description: What you get at the end of three or four hours of braising is an apricot-onion-lamb fat jam that tastes, as you might expect, pretty incredible when slathered onto your fork-tender, juicy lamb ribs.
notes: Notes: If you do find yourself with a pool of rendered lamb fat in your roasting pan, consider collecting it for future use, in something like light and fluffy biscuits, which I usually make with butter, but which are very good with lamb fat, lard, or tallow.
author: Chichi Wang
